claims.statement: Session branches follow the convention open-inspect/{session-id}: generateBranchName derives a PR head branch from a session id and extractSessionIdFromBranch reverses it; the webhook miss-path uses the reverse derivation only as a guarded fallback.

resolveHeadBranchForPr resolves the PR source branch with deterministic precedence - requested headBranch (request), the target repo's stored working branch (session), then the generated open-inspect/{sessionId} branch - skipping candidates that equal the base branch and sanitizing each candidate conservatively; invalid names fall through to the generated branch.

sanitizeBranchName rejects HEAD, leading/trailing slashes or dots, whitespace, '..', '@{', and git-ref control characters such as ~^:?*[\], returning null; the PR service returns 400 when the resolved head does not sanitize.

PR creation is orchestrated by SessionPullRequestService.createPullRequest in the session DO: it re-resolves the repository target itself (defense in depth at the sandbox-auth boundary), claims the target repo with a DO-instance-scoped in-memory claims set so a concurrent request for the same repo gets 409, and releases the claim in a finally block so a failed creation can be retried.

Membership of the target repository is a security boundary for PR creation: the route is reachable with sandbox auth, so the handler resolves the target against the session's repository list (403 for repos outside the session) and the service re-validates before any provider call.

Branch push for PR creation always uses GitHub App installation credentials (generatePushAuth) because push runs inside the sandbox, which must never hold user OAuth tokens; the push spec embeds the app token in a GitHub-specific remote URL and force-pushes HEAD to refs/heads/{headBranch}.
PR base branch resolution is requested baseBranch, then the repository entry's base branch, then the repository default branch read from the provider at creation time.

PR creation attributes the PR to the prompting user when their OAuth token is usable (resolveAuthForPR decrypts scm_access_token_encrypted and refreshes server-side when near expiry), and falls back to the shared GitHub App token when the user has no usable token - e.g. sessions triggered from integrations like Linear; the PR body always carries a 'Created with [app]' footer.

PR creation requires an active user prompt: getPromptingParticipantForPR returns 400 when no message is processing and 401 when the prompting participant cannot be found, so PR creation cannot be triggered by arbitrary sandbox actors.

The policy is one open PR per head branch: when an open PR already exists for the resolved head, creation force-pushes over its head and reuses it (response updated:true, no new PR created); merged/closed PRs release the head branch and a later call creates a fresh PR (follow-up-after-merge flow).

Reuse candidates are resolved against the provider's live PR state, not artifact recency: a merged/closed live state heals the stale-open artifact mirror and the walk continues to older candidates; when the live read fails, reuse falls back to stored facts because reusing a PR that turns out closed is recoverable while opening a duplicate is not.

Force-push reuse is only allowed when the head branch is the sandbox checkout: an explicitly requested branch or the generated session branch. A stored custom branch reached via fallback (e.g. the top of a stack) holds content the request never saw, so creation fails with 409 directing the user to check out that branch.

An explicitly different requested base creates a parallel PR from the same head (providers allow one open PR per head/base pair); without an explicit base the candidate's base stands, so a stacked PR's base is not treated as the session default and a follow-up call is not read as a retarget.

Legacy pre-lifecycle PR artifacts without a pr number or URL cannot be referenced or verified, so they keep the head branch claimed and later creation returns 409 unless a verifiable PR was already reused.

pull-request-snapshot.ts is the canonical PR lifecycle snapshot mapping shared by creation, the webhook path, and read-through refresh: snapshotToRecord produces the D1 authority record, mergeSnapshotMetadata preserves unknown legacy keys and keeps the legacy state display key current, and preparePullRequestArtifactUpdate rejects snapshots strictly older than the stored providerUpdatedAt and no-ops when nothing materially changed.

The D1 session_pull_requests store is the queryable authority record; its upsert is guarded in SQL so a write whose providerUpdatedAt is strictly older than the stored value is rejected (applied:false), preventing an out-of-order webhook from regressing state; a missing timestamp on either side is authoritative, and a conflicting row for the same PR identity under a different artifact id violates the unique identity index and throws (one record per PR).

SessionPullRequestStore.getByIdentity is the single PR identity boundary: (repository_external_id, pr_number) is canonical and rename/transfer-proof, with case-insensitive (repo_owner, repo_name, pr_number) used only as a legacy fallback for rows that predate external-id capture; the next upsert upgrades those rows in place.

All PR freshness paths follow authority-then-mirror ordering (applyPullRequestSnapshot): the D1 record is upserted first - a snapshot the monotonic guard rejects must never reach the mirror - then the artifact is re-read at apply time and the guarded mirror write is performed, returning the artifact_updated payload for the caller to broadcast; a thrown (not rejected) upsert is best-effort and the mirror still updates, with read-through or redelivery repairing D1.

Webhook PR lifecycle tracking piggybacks the /internal/github-event forward in waitUntil and is additive and best-effort: every failure is logged and swallowed so it never affects automation matching; the hit path updates the correlated record and mirrors the snapshot into the owning session DO, and a rejected (stale) D1 write never reaches the mirror.

Webhook correlation is identity-first via (repository_external_id, pr_number); the branch-name fallback is guarded: the derived session must exist AND already be associated with the event's repository, the session must hold a matching DO pr artifact (preferring the one carrying the webhook's PR number over number-less legacy metadata), and cross-repository fork heads are dropped as not-ours.

Read-through refresh (refreshSessionPullRequests) runs on session open and on the manual sync action: each PR artifact is re-read from the provider app-authed, then authority-then-mirror applies the snapshot; it is the only freshness path that reads the provider directly and the only one required when the bot is off, and the manual sync endpoint returns 202 and runs in the background.

The in-sandbox git credential helper (git_credential_helper.py) fetches fresh short-lived credentials per git operation from POST /sessions/:id/scm-credentials, sandbox-authenticated; it caches to /run/oi/scm-creds.json (0600) until within 5 minutes of expiry, serializes concurrent refreshes with an advisory lock, and never uses the cache as a fallback for a failed refresh - a rejected control-plane call exits non-zero because stale tokens silently authenticating are worse than visible failures.

The credential helper scopes served credentials by protocol and host only: protocol must be https and host must equal VCS_HOST (default github.com), so a malicious submodule URL or ls-remote against an attacker host cannot exfiltrate the installation token; it deliberately does not scope to the session repo because setup/start hooks may clone sibling private repositories.

The /sessions/:id/scm-credentials route enforces sandbox authentication bound to the session (SCM_CREDENTIALS_ROUTE): user and service credentials are rejected and a sandbox token bound to another session is rejected; ScmCredentialsService mints through generateCredentialHelperAuth, which for GitHub returns username x-access-token plus a freshly minted installation token with its expiry, mapping permanent provider errors to 500 and transient to 502, and never logs the password.

Image-build sandboxes have no control plane to refresh against: the manager injects VCS_CLONE_TOKEN and the helper treats it as good for one hour, refusing the env fallback whenever a control-plane context is present but incomplete (CONTROL_PLANE_URL, SANDBOX_AUTH_TOKEN, or SESSION_CONFIG sessionId missing).

resolveGitHubCredentialAuthority selects the credential store for a user's GitHub identity: a browser user must never silently fall back to the legacy token store when authentication provenance is missing - linked GitHub accounts are enumerated from the verified principal's account client only when an SCM workflow requests them, and service actors are the only transitional callers retaining the legacy authority.

The GitHub Autofix pipeline ingresses issue_comment (created, skipping bot mentions) and pull_request_review (submitted) payloads into GitHubAutofixEnvelopes at the github-bot, sends them to a queue named open-inspect-github-autofix-*, and the control-plane worker consumes them via AutofixQueueConsumer: parse failures retry, success acks, transient failures retry up to 5 delivery attempts, and permanent provider errors mark the feedback failed and ack immediately.

AutofixService.process is an idempotent state machine persisted per feedback in pr_autofix_feedback keyed github:{kind}:{providerObjectId}: receive (insert-or-update, incrementing delivery count), correlate to the owning session via SessionPullRequestStore identity, skip untracked PRs, recover an ambiguous prior dispatch via lookup_feedback, resolve eligibility against integration settings and the provider's open/live PR state, and dispatch an enqueue_feedback command to the session DO's /internal/autofix endpoint; enqueued/duplicate mark queued, rejected (session_closed/queue_full/attempt_limit) marks skipped.

Autofix eligibility rules: feedback from the bot itself is only actionable when openInspectReviewsEnabled is set for reviews; explicit @bot mentions on PR comments are skipped; human authors must have write permission on the repo (verified via the provider); other bot authors must be in allowedReviewBots; only COMMENTED and CHANGES_REQUESTED review states with non-empty content are actionable, and empty feedback and unsupported author types are skipped.

The Autofix prompt wraps feedback (body, review comments with truncated diff hunks of 4000 chars) in <github_feedback_data> and instructs the agent to treat it as untrusted review data; reviews over 100 comments or prompts over 200,000 bytes are rejected as permanent errors.

Session-side admission (message queue) creates a participant for the GitHub feedback author and admits the message transactionally: duplicates by feedback key, closed sessions, queue-full, and - when maxAttemptsPerPrPer24Hours is configured - an attempt count for that PR key within the rolling 24-hour window are rejected; the default cap is 30 and null disables it; successful enqueue redrives the pending queue so the session wakes.

Commit signing in the sandbox is a sibling in-sandbox flow: GitSigningRuntime fetches the session's commit-signing configuration over GET /sessions/:id/commit-signing and translates an enabled configuration into per-repo git config (SSH-signing format gpg.ssh.program, committer identity, commit.gpgsign true) or unsets signing keys when disabled, falling back to an unsigned author identity, with bounded errors that never include secret configuration values.
